extracted.intended_audience: researchers or academic leaders applying for UK Global Talent visa via UKRI endorsement
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researchers and academic leaders seeking UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) endorsement as part of a Global Talent visa application, specifying eligibility, required documents, and application timings. Focused on applicants working on grants/awards from UKRI-endorsed funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant awarded by an organisation on the list of endorsed funders
rubrics_metrics.description: Your grant must have been awarded by an organisation on the list of endorsed funders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only grants from organisations that appear on UKRI’s endorsed funders list qualify for this endorsement route.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employing or hosting organisation approved by UKRI
rubrics_metrics.description: The organisation employing or hosting you must be approved by UKRI. The organisation must be in the UK (but you can do research abroad).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your employer/host must hold UKRI approval; physical presence of the organisation is required in the UK even if your research activity takes place overseas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum remaining employment/hosting contract length
rubrics_metrics.description: You must have at least 1 year left on your employment contract or hosting agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endorsement expects an existing commitment of at least one year remaining at the time of application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum time allocation to the grant
rubrics_metrics.description: You must spend at least half of your time working on the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For principal investigators or co-investigators, time across more than one grant can be combined so long as, in total, they constitute at least half of your working time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum grant value and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be working on a grant worth at least £30,000 that covers at least 2 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grant’s financial value and duration criteria are cumulative: both the monetary threshold (£30,000) and the minimum term (2 years) must be met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible grant type
rubrics_metrics.description: You must have either a one-off grant or award, or a ‘renewable’ award with regular peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewable awards are acceptable provided they undergo regular peer review; one-off payments that meet value/duration rules are also acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role requirement: lead OR contribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Along with your grant or award you must either lead a unique research or innovation project, or contribute to research in developing new technology or methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must fit one of these two role pathways (leadership vs contributory technical/methodological role) in relation to the grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leading a project — qualifications and participation
rubrics_metrics.description: If you’re leading a unique research or innovation project you must have a PhD or equivalent research experience (including clinical and industrial research) and have actively participated in your relevant field of research within a university, research institution or industrial setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrable research experience equivalent to a PhD counts; participation in academic, institutional, clinical or industrial research contexts is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leading a project — connection to the grant application
rubrics_metrics.description: If leading, you must either be named on the research grant application or have your job title on the research grant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being explicitly associated with the grant application (named or by job title) is required to verify your leadership role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributing to research — experience requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you will contribute to research in developing new technology or methodology you must have research experience within a university, research institution or industrial setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior research experience in relevant settings is required even for contributory roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributing to research — qualifications alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: If contributing, you must also either have a UK bachelor’s degree, have an equivalent overseas research degree, or have equivalent research experience (including clinical and industrial research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualification can be satisfied by formal degree credentials or equivalent practical research experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for recent career breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: If you’ve recently taken time away from actively participating in your relevant field of research (for example a career break or parental leave), and you’ll be returning to your employment, you’ll still be eligible for the Global Talent visa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Career breaks do not automatically disqualify applicants; eligibility is retained when returning to the employment/hosting arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: If grant is on UKRI approved award databases — provide link and database confirmations
rubrics_metrics.description: If your grant or award is on the list of UKRI approved award databases, you must provide a link to it in your endorsement application. The database must confirm the grant or award is worth at least £30,000, covers at least 2 years, and is either a one-off funding payment or a ‘renewable’ award with regular peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the approved database entry as documentary proof that the grant meets financial, duration and type criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: If grant not on database — letter from endorsed funder required
rubrics_metrics.description: If your grant or award is not included on the database, you’ll need a letter from your endorsed funder instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The funder’s letter should verify the grant’s value, duration and peer-review/renewable status as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required HR (or equivalent) letter content from employer/host
rubrics_metrics.description: You need to provide a letter from the director of human resources (or equivalent) at the organisation where you’re working that states: the name of the position and department where you work; that you have accepted the job offer or hosting agreement; that you are essential to the grant; that you will be spending at least half of your agreed working time on the grant; and details of the fair recruitment process, if you were not specifically named on the grant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This employer/host letter must cover all listed points; include fair recruitment details where applicable to explain how you were selected or named.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide documents for all grants used in the application
rubrics_metrics.description: You need to provide documents for all grants you’re using for your endorsement application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using multiple grants to meet the 'half time' or funding criteria, supply supporting documentation for each one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timing and decision expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply for endorsement once you have the documents — you’ll usually get a decision within 2 weeks. You can apply for the Global Talent visa at the same time as you apply for endorsement, or after endorsement is confirmed. You’ll get a visa response within 3 weeks if you’re outside the UK, and 8 weeks if you’re inside the UK. If your permission to stay in the UK is about to expire, applying for the visa will extend it until you’ve been given a decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan timing according to expected decision windows; applying for the visa can protect immigration status while awaiting outcome.
